subject: general
question: India launched its National Red List Roadmap at which of the following international events in 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**IUCN World Conservation Congress**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India officially launched its **National Red List Roadmap** during the **IUCN World Conservation Congress (WCC)** held in **2025**. This roadmap serves as a strategic document to guide the assessment of the conservation status of species found within **India**.
 
• The initiative is a collaborative effort led by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)**, in partnership with global conservation bodies. It aims to apply the **IUCN Red List Categories and Criteria** at the national level to identify species at the highest risk of **extinction**.
 
• The primary objective of the **National Red List Roadmap** is to ensure that conservation efforts are data-driven. By creating a national database, India can prioritize funding and protection for species classified as **Critically Endangered** or **Endangered** under national standards.
 
• This roadmap is crucial for fulfilling India’s obligations under the **Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework**, specifically **Target 4**, which focuses on halting species extinction and managing human-wildlife conflict.
 
• The **2025 Congress** in **Abu Dhabi, UAE**, provided the international platform for India to showcase its scientific rigor in biodiversity monitoring, involving organizations like the **Zoological Survey of India (ZSI)** and the **Botanical Survey of India (BSI)**. ***Hence, the correct answer is IUCN World Conservation Congress.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **IUCN (International Union for Conservation of Nature):** 
 
 
• Established in **1948**, it is the world’s largest environmental network, composed of both **government** and **civil society** organizations.
 
• Its headquarters is located in **Gland, Switzerland**. The organization acts as an advisor to the **United Nations** and helps implement international conventions.
 
 
 
• **IUCN Red List of Threatened Species:** 
 
 
• First established in **1964**, it is the global standard for evaluating the extinction risk of species. It classifies species into categories such as **Vulnerable**, **Endangered**, and **Critically Endangered**.
 
• The **Red List** is updated periodically and serves as a "health check" for the planet's **biodiversity**.
 
 
 
• **IUCN World Conservation Congress (WCC):** 
 
 
• This event is held every **four years** and is often referred to as the "Olympics of Conservation." The **2025** session in **Abu Dhabi** focused heavily on **nature-based solutions** and **climate resilience**.
 
• It brings together thousands of delegates to vote on **motions** that set the global agenda for conservation policy.
 
 
 
• **National Red List vs. Global Red List:** 
 
 
• While the global list assesses species across their entire range, a **National Red List** focuses on the status of a species within a specific country's **borders**.
 
• A species might be **Least Concern** globally but **Critically Endangered** within India due to localized threats like **habitat loss** or **poaching**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Biodiversity in India:** India is recognized as one of the **17 mega-diverse** countries in the world, harboring approximately **7-8%** of all recorded species. Notable endemics include the **Asiatic Lion** and the **Sangai Deer**.
 
• **Legal Framework:** The data generated through the **National Red List Roadmap** will inform the schedules of the **Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972**, ensuring legal protection matches the biological threat level.
 
• **Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF):** Adopted in **2022**, the framework sets **23 targets** for **2030**, including the protection of **30%** of the world’s land and oceans (the **30x30 target**).
 
• **Other Options Context:** The **UN Climate Change Conference (COP30)** in **Brazil** primarily focuses on **carbon emissions** and the **Paris Agreement**, whereas the **IUCN WCC** is specifically dedicated to **species conservation**.
